Portents Gather.
Scene one.
The Restless Night.
Odysseus lies awake in the portico, angered by disloyal maids slipping out to the suitors.
Why you doubts after reaching home?
I am with you, and I never leave you.
If fifty companies of men stood against us with spears, you would drive off their cattle by morning.
Sleep now.
I lay it on your eyes myself.
Hear me, for death, and dreams that Odysseus lies beside her.

scenes.card: Herdsmen arrive for a festival: the goatherd insults the beggar, but a loyal cowherd greets him warmly.

subs.text: Scene three.
The Herdsmen Arrive.
Eurycleia wakes the household and servants prepare the hall for Apollo's feast day.
Good morning, stranger.
Do the men treat you any better today, or is the house still the house it was?
Still here, dog?
Still working the doorway for scraps?
Forgive me, father.
My eyes run when I look at you.
My master would wear your rags now, if he lives.
Herdsman, mark what I say, and let the gods hear it.
Before you drive your cattle home again, Odysseus will stand in this house,
and you will see with your own eyes the suitors killed.

scenes.title: The Hall of Death
scenes.card: The suitors laugh wildly while the prophet sees them covered in blood and shadow, and warns they are doomed.

subs.text: Scene five.
The Hall of Death.
Athena drives the suitors into uncontrollable laughter while their meat drips blood in their vision.
They laugh with jaws that will not close, and the meat they lift is dripping blood,
and the tears run down their faces while they laugh.
Theoclymenus sees darkness covering them, ghosts crowding the court, and blood on the walls.
Announces their approaching destruction and leaves when they mock him.
Telemachus and Odysseus watch one another across the doomed feast.

sign.operation: One wide of the feast with walls running with blood and shades in the doorway, not marked as vision; the suitors keep laughing.

scenes.world: a dim stone banquet hall with timber roof beams, lit only by hearth fire and oil lamps, silent-era costume drama look; the same feast going wrong, faces harsh in low firelight, smoke thickening.

captain.asks: One wide of the feast running with blood and shades in the doorway, unmarked as vision, while laughter continues.
diagnosis: The banquet footage is the strongest feast in the book: long tables, men eating with open jaws.
But it is tuxedos and restaurant chairs; blood on the walls is never seen.
The seer is a face of eyes only; the exchanged look at the end is the same eye stock reused.

prologue: It is the night before the contest. The king lies awake, unsure he can defeat so many men, while the gods send warning signs of what is coming.

carry: Every sign points to death for the suitors, and they laugh it off.
